sections.html: Gnathocharax steindachneri attains a maximum length of only 5 cm and belongs to the closer relationship to the freshwater barracudas (Acestrorhynchus), which is clearly visible by the structure of the fangs and teeth.

In the natural habitat of the cardinal tetra food sources are very scarce. So it is really astonishing how many species can exist there. However, many of them stay very small. Even a predatory species of that biotope is such a dwarf: Gnathocharax steindachneri.

Most probably the species feeds on fish and insect larvae in the wild. In the aquarium the fish feed readily on any type of usual fish food, even dry food is taken from the very first day on, despite the specialized dentition.

Gnathocharax is not dangerous for other fishes larger than approx. 1 cm. It is perfectly suitable for community tanks with cardinals and other tetras. Here Gnathocharax loves to swim along with conspecifics in the upper third of the water column.
